content.title: Who won Oscars 2026 awards? Best Picture, Best Actress winners, more
content.text: “In 1975, the Oscar nominees for Best Picture were 'Dog Day Afternoon,' 'One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest,' 'Jaws,' 'Nashville' and 'Barry Lyndon.' There is no best among them. There is just what their mood might be that day. But we’re happy to be part of this a wonderful, wonderful journey,” Anderson said.He then closed it our with the best directive for the room: “You guys, let’s have a martini, let’s party.” Jessie Buckley wins Best Actress for ‘Hamnet’ 10:32 p.m.: Jessie Buckley, in one of tonight’s few seemingly guaranteed wins, takes home the Oscar for Best Actress for her emotional performance as Agnes in “Hamnet.” Buckley practically swept awards season, and tonight marks her first win.Article continues below this ad“This is really something,” said an awed Buckley, in shock. “It’s Mother’s Day in the U.K., so I would like to dedicate this to the beautiful chaos of a mother’s heart.” Michael B. Jordan earns Best Actor Oscar for his dual roles in 'Sinners' 10:23 p.m.: First-time Oscar nominee Michael B. Jordan won Best Actor for playing twins Smoke and Stack in Ryan Coogler’s “Sinners.”In his acceptance speech, he called out his mom — his date to every awards ceremony — and his longtime collaborator, Ryan Coogler.Article continues below this ad“Thank you for betting on the culture and betting on original ideas,” Jordan told Coogler.He then called out the Black actors who won before him, expressing gratitude for being “amongst my ancestors, amongst my guys.” Paul Thomas Anderson wins Best Director for 'One Battle After Another' 10:18 p.m.: “You make a guy work hard for these,” Paul Thomas Anderson joked while accepting his first-ever award for directing.Article continues below this ad“This is a wonderful gift, and I’m so happy to call movies home,” Anderson said.PTA’s Best Director win has been long-awaited; he was previously nominated in this category for “There Will Be Blood,” “Phantom Thread” and “Licorice Pizza.” ‘Golden’ from ‘KPop Demon Hunters’ takes home gold 10:14 p.m.: A frontrunner since the earworm dominated the charts and every parents’ Spotify, “Golden” from “Kpop Demon Hunters” was crowned Best Original Song. Co-writers EJAE, who also provided the singing voice for Rumi, and Mark Sonnenblick accepted the gold-plated statue.Article continues below this ad“Growing up, people make fun of me, for liking K-Pop, but now everyone’s singing ourselves all the Korean lyrics from 'Golden,'” said Ejae, emotion filling her voice. Though K-Pop as a genre has dominated the globe, this marks the first time a K-Pop song has won this award. 'Sentimental Value' wins Best International Feature 10:07 p.m.: Director Joachim Trier’s “Sentimental Value,” starring Stellan Skarsgård, Renate Reinsve and Elle Fanning, won for Best International Feature. This marks Trier’s first Oscar.Article continues below this ad“I’m just a film nerd from Norway,” Trier said. “I make films to feel at home with people.”He then paraphrased James Baldwin: “Let us remember that all adults are responsible for all children. Let’s not vote for politicians who don’t take this seriously into account.” Trier’s 2021 romantic dramedy “Worst Person in the World,” also starring Reinsve, was nominated in this category at the 2022 Academy Awards. 'Golden' transforms 2026 Oscars into a K-Pop concert 10:01 p.m.: Traditional Korean song and dance opened “Golden” from “KPop Demon Hunters.” The bright, yet short, performance had the audience dancing with light-up globe wands in their seats. Article continues below this ad 'Sinners' cinematographer makes Oscars history 9:52 p.m.: Autumn Durald Arkapaw’s Best Cinematography win makes her the first woman to win the award in the Oscars’ 98-year history. Even her nomination was historic — she is the first woman of color to even be nominated.“I want all the women in the room to stand up, because I feel like I don’t get here without you guys,” Arkapaw said. “Moments like this happen because of you guys.” 'One Battle After Another' wins film Best Film Editing 9:48 p.m.: Andy Jurgensen won the Oscar for Best Film Editing for his work on Paul Thomas Anderson’s “One Battle After Another.”Article continues below this ad 'Sinners,' Ludwig Göransson win Best Original Score, 'F1' wins Best Sound 9:37 p.m.: Ludwig Göransson won for his blues-infused score for “Sinners.” He previously won for his work on “Black Panther” and “Oppenheimer.”Best Sound went to “F1,” the Brad Pitt-led racing drama. Gareth John, Al Nelson, Gwendolyn Yates Whittle, Gary A. Rizzo and Juan Peralta accepted the award. 'Mr. Nobody Against Putin' takes home Oscar for Best Documentary Feature 9:27 p.m.: “Mr. Nobody Against Putin,” which follows a Russian primary school teacher whose work with his students simultaneously captured the Putin administration’s propaganda roll out after the 2022 invasion of Ukraine, won for Best Documentary Feature.Article continues below this adWhile the evening’s political commentary has been largely relegated to host Conan O’Brien, the documentary categories have bucked the trend. After “All the Empty Rooms” win, the filmmakers of “Mr. Nobody Against Putin” continued calling out injustices.“'Mr. Nobody Against Putin' is about how you lose your country,” said director David Borenstein. “What we saw when working with this footage that you it’s that you lose it through countless small, little acts of complicity. When we act complicit, when a government murders people on the streets of our major cities, when we don’t say anything, when oligarchs take over the media and control how we can produce it and consume it, we all face a moral choice. Luckily, even a nobody is more powerful than you think.” Schenectady-raised director wins Oscar for 'All the Empty Rooms' 9:20 p.m.: Joshua Seftel, born and raised in Schenectady, won for his work on the harrowing short documentary “All the Empty Rooms.”Article continues below this adSeftel, Troy-based veteran journalist Steve Hartman and photographer Lou Bopp teamed up for the film, which follows Hartman and Bopp’s sobering mission to memorialize the bedrooms of children who died in school shootings. For a deeper dive into how this poignant documentary came to be, check out our feature here.Much of Seftel’s allotted speech time was given to Gloria Cazaes, the mother of Jackie, a student murdered at the Uvalde school shooting at Robb Elementary.“Jackie is more than just a headline. She is our light and our life,” Cazares said. “Gun violence is now the number one cause of death in kids and teens. We believe that if the world could see their empty bedrooms, we’d be a different America.”This is Seftel’s first win. He was previously nominated in the same category for his work on “Stranger at the Gate.”Article continues below this ad 'Frankenstein' wins Best Production Design, 'Avatar' Best Visual Effects at 2026 Oscars 9:09 p.m.: “Frankenstein” won its third Oscar of the evening for Best Production Design. Tamara Deverell and Shane Vieau accepted the award.The Oscar for Best Visual Effects went to “Avatar: Fire and Ash,” the third in James Cameron’s fantasy series. The previous two “Avatar” films have also won this award for their groundbreaking visual effects. Joe Letteri, Richard Baneham, Eric Saindon and Daniel Barrett accepted the award. Billy Crystal, Rachel McAdams, Barbra Streisand honor Rob Reiner, Diane Keaton, Robert Redford during touching In Memoriam 8:59 p.m.: There was no one better to honor the late Rob Reiner than his best friend, Billy Crystal. After listing off Reiner’s incredible filmography — “This Is Spinal Tap,” “When Harry Met Sally,” “Princess Bride,” “Misery,” “Stand By Me,” “A Few Good Men” and so many more — he dipped into a heartfelt remembrance of the good Reiner and his wife Michelle brought into the world, notably their fight for marriage equality.Article continues below this adThen the curtain rose, and actors from Reiner’s career, including Carol Kane, Meg Ryan and John Cusack, were standing hand in hand. The lights dimmed, and the In Memoriam, set to the “Princess Bride” score, launched.Rachel McAdams arrived midway through to acknowledge some of the women lost, including Claudia Carinale, Diane Ladd, Catherine O’Hara and McAdams' “Family Stone” co-star Diane Keaton, calling her “a legend with no end.”After a few more moments of video, Barbra Streisand emerged to reflect on her late co-star Robert Redford. She called him “thoughtful,” “bold,” and an “intellectual cowboy.” She then she sang the chorus from “The Way We Were” to briefly, and sweetly, cap off the tribute.It was simple, but after a year of such loss, perfect. No onstage singers to pan to, just time to sit and remember the giants who shaped cinema distraction-free. The Oscars don’t always get the In Memoriam right, but this year, they did.Article continues below this ad 'Sinners' wins first Oscar of the night for Best Original Screenplay 8:38 p.m.: And following suit, Ryan Coogler wins his first Oscar for Best Original Screenplay for for his vampiric epic. “Sinners” provided an incisive look at racism in the South through a supernatural, musical lens. The film, like “One Battle Another,” is also a contender for Best Picture. 'One Battle After Another,' Paul Thomas Anderson win Best Adapted Screenplay 8:36 p.m.: Paul Thomas Anderson wins his first Oscar for his loose adaptation of “Vineland” by Thomas Pynchon.Article continues below this ad“I owe a huge debt of admiration and of Thomas Pynchon. Any writer knows that you either beg for forgiveness, or your special thanks is really to your family and the people that you share a roof with who put up with what it means to live with a writer,” Anderson said, before calling out his partner Maya Rudolph. “I wrote this movie for my kids to say sorry for the housekeeping mess that we left in this world, and we’re handing off to them. But also with the encouragement that they will be the generation that hopefully brings us some common sense and decency.” Sean Penn, absent from ceremony wins Best Supporting Actor for 'One Battle After Another' 8:26 p.m.: Sean Penn may not have come to the Academy Awards, but that didn’t stop him from snagging his third Oscar for Col. Steven J. Lockjaw, the antagonist in “One Battle After Another.”Penn’s absence isn’t a surprise — he skipped the BAFTAs and Actor Awards too. He is consistent, at least.Article continues below this ad Short films 'The Singers,' 'Two People Exchanging Saliva' tie for Best Live-Action Short, marking the 7th tie in Oscars history 8:20 p.m.: While feature-length works always dominate the Academy Awards ceremony, short films also get much-deserved recognition. And this year, we had a tie for Best Live-Action Short: “The Singers” and “Two People Exchanging Saliva”There have only been six ties before tonight. The last tie was in 2013 when “Zero Dark Thirty” and “Skyfall” tied for Best Sound Editing.Earlier this evening, “The Girl Who Cried Pearls” won Best Animated Short. Best Casting, the Oscar’s new category, goes to 'One Battle After Another' 8:06 p.m.: Paul Mescal, Gwyneth Paltrow, Chase Infiniti, Wagner Moura and Delroy Lindo introduced each of the nominees for this year’s new category, Best Casting.Article continues below this ad“One Battle After Another” casting director Cassandra Kulukundis won the inaugural award.“For the casting directors who fought tirelessly to make it happen despite everything in their way, I dedicate this to you, and to casting directors who never got a chance to get up here, who didn’t even get a chance to get their name on the movie,” Kulukundis said. This category was created to honor casting directors’ “essential role in filmmaking,” per Academy CEO Bill Kramer in a 2024 release announcing the addition. It’s the first new one in 24 years.At the 2028 Oscars (which will also be the 100th Academy Awards), another new category will premiere: Best Stunt Design. Tom Cruise better ride a motorcycle, speeding off a helicopter and over a pit of fire to present the long overdue award when the time comes.Article continues below this ad 'Devil Wears Prada 2' star Anne Hathaway, Vogue’s Anna Wintour announce 'Frankenstein' for Best Costume Design, Best Makeup and Hairstyling 7:56 p.m.: Guillermo del Toro’s “Frankenstein” took home the awards for Best Costume Design, awarded to designer Kate Hawley, and Best Makeup and Hairstyling, awarded to Mike Hill, Jordan Samuel and Cliona Furey. 'Sinners' takes over the Dolby Theatre to recreate 'I Lied to You' scene live 7:41 p.m.: The standing ovation following “Sinners” explosive performance of “I Lied to You” was well deserved. Star Miles Canton and song co-writer Raphael Saadiq were joined by a star-studded ensemble of artists including Eric Gales, Buddy Guy, Brittany Howard, Christone “Kingfish” Ingram, Jayme Lawson, Li Jun Li, Bobby Rush, Shaboozey and Alice Smith. And though the camera didn’t pan to Timothée Chalamet when ballerina Misty Copeland emerged in “Firebird” glory, it’s fine — seeing the trailblazer dancing en pointe less than three months after hip replacement surgery was pure magic. Article continues below this ad 'KPop Demon Hunters' wins Oscar for Best Animated Feature 7:35 p.m.: Everything is, in fact, “Golden” for the creators of “KPop Demon Hunters,” which won this year’s Oscar for Best Animated Feature. Co-directors Maggie Kang and Chris Appelhans and producer Michelle L.M. Wong accepted the award.“for those of you who look like me, I’m so sorry that it took us so long to see us in a movie. But it is here,” said Kang, choked with emotion. “And that means that the next generation don’t have to go long. This is for Korea and for Koreans everywhere.” Amy Madigan wins Best Supporting Actress for Aunt Gladys in 'Weapons' 7:25 p.m.: No hairy bewitchment needed here for Amy Madigan’s Oscar win. Her role as the mysterious Aunt Gladys in “Weapons” became an instant audience favorite (she’s even getting a prequel!). Article continues below this adA shocked Madigan started off with an infectious cackle.“Everyone has ask it’s been 40 years, and, you know, what’s different about this time? What’s different about this little gold guy,” a “flummoxed” Madigan began.Though this marks Madigan’s first win, this is her second Oscar nomination. She was a Best Supporting Actress nominee 40 years ago for her role in “Twice in a Lifetime.”She ended teary-eyed thanking husband Ed Harris.Article continues below this ad Host Conan O’Brien kicks off 2026 Oscars with digs at AI, Netflix, Timothée Chalamet 7:19 p.m.: Conan O’Brien launched the night in a drag homage to Aunt Gladys from “Weapons” while a hoard of children running too fast, too furious chased him through the night’s biggest nominee. The pre-recorded bits transformed to a real-life sprint down the carpet and up the stage where he went into his opening monologue.“I’m Conan O’Brien, and I’m proud to be the last human host,” Conan joked, likely a nod to the growing presence of AI.Timothée Chalamet’s controversial comments about ballet and opera were instantly addressed, with O’Brien joking there was extra security due to reports of the ballet and opera communities coordinating an attack.Article continues below this ad“I’m warning you tonight could get political. If that makes you uncomfortable, there is an alternate Oscars hosted by Kid Rock. It’s at Dave & Busters down the street,” said O’Brien, digging at the alternate Super Bowl Half Time show that emerged amid conservative uproar over Bad Bunny.He also made digs at Netflix CEO Ted Sarandos (“This is his first time in a theater!”) and the healthcare system (using “Hamnet’s” forest-set birth scene as an example of affordable healthcare).We also got a new Leo meme, though jury’s out on whether it’ll go viral, and Michael B. Jordan as the seat filler (a gag that I could see running throughout the night).O’Brien then got serious, acknowledging the turmoil sweeping the globe and pointing to the Oscars — and its “ideals of global artistry, collaboration, resilience, and rarest of qualities today, optimism” — as something to celebrate.Article continues below this adBut don’t worry, the humor kicked back up. When Josh Groban promised silliness early today, he was not lying. Joined by the Los Angeles Master Chorale, Groban serenaded a crowned Conan with an ode to the medieval era. Oscars statues made in the Hudson Valley 6:54 p.m.: It’s five minutes until showtime for the 2026 Oscars, and soon the titular statues will be handed out to tonight’s winners. Though the ceremony is in Hollywood, the famous awards are made in the Hudson Valley’s Orange County. UAP Polich Tallix, based in Rock Tavern, has overseen Oscars production since 2015. ‘KPop Demon Hunters,’ ‘Sinners’ and more poised to make Oscars history 6:17 p.m.: “Golden” is the first K-Pop song nominated for Best Original Song. On the red carpet, co-writer Ejae got emotional reflecting on the possibility of making history at tonight’s ceremony.Article continues below this ad“To see our culture and song loved by so many is a dream come true,” Ejae told E! during a red carpet interview.More nominees are also on the cusp of Oscars’s history. “Sinners'” cinematographer Autumn Durald Arkapaw could become the first woman in the awards' 98-year-history to win Best Cinematography, and the film’s record-breaking 16 nominations means it could break the record for most awards won by a film. “Titanic,” “Ben-Hur” and “Lord of the Rings: Return of the King” are the current record holders at 11 each. Additionally, Chloé Zhao could become the only woman to have won two Best Director awards if she wins for “Hamnet.” Rose Byrne joined by husband Bobby Cannavale on the Oscars red carpet 5:32 p.m.: With no major reptile expos to distract him, Bobby Cannavale is at the Oscars with his wife Rose Byrne. Byrne is nominated for Best Actress for her intense role in “If I Had Legs I’d Kick You.” The pair went viral during the Golden Globes in January when Byrne, during her acceptance speech for Best Actress in a Comedy or Musical, revealed her husband was missing in action because he was buying their family a pet bearded dragon at a New Jersey expo.Article continues below this ad Chase Infiniti, Rose Byrne and more to present 2026 Oscars awards alongside host Conan O’Brien 5:13 p.m.: The Academy Awards lined up a star-studded roster of past winners, current nominees and A-Listers to announce this evening’s awards. Tonight’s presenters include Will Arnett, Javier Bardem, Adrien Brody, Rose Byrne, Priyanka Chopra Jonas, Kieran Culkin, Robert Downey Jr., Chris Evans, Anne Hathaway, Chase Infiniti, Nicole Kidman, Jimmy Kimmel, Delroy Lindo, Mikey Madison, Paul Mescal, Ewan McGregor, Demi Moore, Wagner Moura, Kumail Nanjiani, Gwyneth Paltrow, Pedro Pascal, Bill Pullman, Lewis Pullman, Maya Rudolph, Channing Tatum, Zoe Saldaña and Sigourney Weaver.Matt Berry, known for his role of vampire Laszlo in the comedy series “What We Do in the Shadows,” will be the evening’s announcer. Article continues below this ad ‘KPop Demon Hunter,’ ‘Sinners’ and ‘Heated Rivalry’ arrive on the Oscars 2026 red carpet 4:40 p.m.: Film’s biggest night isn’t strictly reserved for movie stars only. “Heated Rivalry” star Hudson Williams just arrived, alongside some of the stars of “Sinners” and “KPop Demon Hunters.” Who is performing at the 2026 Oscars? 4:28 p.m.: Josh Groban, one of tonight’s musical performers, just made a red carpet promise for something “absolutely silly” with his performance alongside the Los Angeles Master Chorale and Conan O’Brien tonight.Article continues below this adThis year, only two of the five Best Original Song nominees will be performed: “Golden” from “KPop Demon Hunters” and “I Lied to You” from “Sinners.” But both promise to be fully staged showstoppers. Ejae, Audrey Nuna and Rei Ami, the singing voices of the fictional Huntr/x, will reunite to celebrate “KPop Demon Hunters” and the rich cultural history behind the film. Every performance of the chart-topping earworm has been electric, so expect a KPop spectacle.“I Lied to You” will not only feature “Sinners” star Miles Canton and song co-writer Raphael Saadiq but also a star-studded ensemble of artists including Eric Gales, Buddy Guy, Brittany Howard, Christone “Kingfish” Ingram, Jayme Lawson, Li Jun Li, Bobby Rush, Shaboozey, Alice Smith and Misty Copeland, former principal dancer for American Ballet Theatre. I expect at least one camera pan to Timothée Chalamet as she dances, minimum.Also, rumors have circulated that Barbra Streisand may perform a tribute to “The Way We Were” co-star, the late Robert Redford.Article continues below this ad As the Oscars 2026 red carpet kicks off, here are the races to watch 4:08 p.m.: The stars have slowly started to arrive for one of the biggest nights of the year: the Academy Awards.For those who don’t make it their spreadsheet-mapped mission to watch as many awards contenders as possible (or for those who do!), here are the biggest races to watch tonight in what is one of the most unpredictable Oscars in recent history.At 16 nominations, “Sinners” shattered the record for most nominations received by a film. It’s in a tight race against Paul Thomas Anderson’s “One Battle After Another” for Best Picture; director Ryan Coogler is also facing off against PTA for Best Director.Article continues below this ad
